text:
Matthew Knies played 240 games for the Maple Leafs, and tonight he plays his first in Toronto as a Blue Jacket. He returns to a building in a bad way. The Leafs are winless in eight (0-7-1), outscored 33-15, and Thursday's version was the cruelest: up 3-0 on the Kings, beaten in a shootout. Coach Jim Hiller is already being asked about his job security, which tells you where this has gone.

The streak isn't bad luck. Toronto has taken 43% of the expected goals during it (expected goals measure the quality of chances). Sergei Bobrovsky is .827 over his last five starts, all losses, and 7.6 goals worse than expected. Kirill Marchenko is on injured reserve (ESPN estimates Nov. 27), and rookie Gavin McKenna has taken his spot on William Nylander's line. Nylander's effort, meanwhile, is being questioned out loud by Paul Bissonnette. Our simulations now give the Leafs a 2.4% playoff chance. Auston Matthews is still 42% to score in our numbers, the best on either side.

Columbus isn't much happier, just a little less unhappy. The Blue Jackets snapped a five-game winless run with a 4-2 win in Chicago on Thursday, but they're 1-4-0 in their last five and at 7% for the playoffs. Sean Monahan is out (ESPN estimates Nov. 25) and Conor Garland is on injured reserve; Adam Fantilli moved beside Valeri Nichushkin. Steven Lorentz, 151 games a Leaf, also makes his first trip back. Kent Johnson has points in four straight.

Here's what stands out: our numbers have the visitors ahead in expected goals, 3.37 to 2.88. Both of our Sleepers are Blue Jackets. Mathieu Olivier is pointless in seven straight despite 2.8 expected goals, one goal from 50 for his career, and 21% to score tonight; Charlie Coyle is 61% for a point against a season pace of 51%, because his line creates chances. Toronto won the first meeting 6-2 on Oct. 20, back when that was normal.
headline: Knies comes home to a Leafs team that can't win
